judgements.justification: B's VyNV wrongly said the paper states no contributions (lines 96-103 list three), and that fed the meta-review's 'unclear technical contribution' problem; GwuL's wrong claim that NCSNv2 is not a denoiser underlies B's crediting of the images to the prior. No A reviewer made these errors.
A's AC gave a spotlight over 5, 8, 7, 7 without arguing the tier, conceding 'the innovation over [19] isn't strong enough' and resting on its own view that the figures 'speak for themselves'.

A's thin YnSg 7 was not enthusiastic praise (it said 'I don't know' on significance and made a critical Stein point); B's kSnH 7 on pictures that 'look really nice' fell to 5 and did not carry weight. R12 covers YnSg.

The authors conceded to B's GwuL that the derivation assumes no dependence between the image and the null space of H, an unbounded approximation; on A's forum they never said so, and A's nVFq thought the assumption held.
A knew from nVFq, y4bh and YnSg that the paper had no comparison with any method, accepted the PnP/RED comparison on promise, and its meta-review omitted the missing baselines.
After the rebuttal A's nVFq rose from a reject score to 5, while B's d1T5, kSnH and VyNV each fell two points; the moves went in opposite directions and widened the gap.

Only B asked whether the SVD sampler beats prior samplers on the same NCSNv2 prior, treated the admitted approximation as a flaw, and credited the image quality to NCSNv2; only A raised novelty over [19] and the missing step-size ablation.
Both committees saw no baseline comparison and a hard Section 3 derivation; A accepted the missing baselines as a revision item and gave a spotlight, while B made them its first ground for rejection.
B's AC took GwuL's points, but all four of B's final ratings were below threshold, so the AC did not resolve a split panel; A's AC followed the majority.
B's d1T5, kSnH and VyNV, none of whom raised baselines in their own reviews, each read the other reviews and dropped two points citing the baselines only GwuL had raised.
The authors misread GwuL's baseline request as a call to compare with Jalal et al. ('I wasn't asking for a comparison to [2]') and never answered GwuL's 2021-09-07 follow-up, and GwuL held 4.
A's YnSg gave 7 at confidence 5 after 2 hours with the summary pasted as the review, said 'I don't know' on significance, never posted in discussion, and the 7 counted toward the spotlight.
B's AC rejected over final ratings 5, 5, 4, 4, all below threshold, so it did not go against a positive majority.
Neither AC stated a positive view yet decided by a mean threshold; A's AC accepted on the majority, and B's AC was negative.
The low scores rested on missing baselines, novelty and derivation clarity, which are central to the contribution.
Both committees read the paper as a posterior-sampling method for inverse problems and judged it as such.
A's only raise came from nVFq at confidence 4 with specific reasons; no reviewer who disclaimed expertise raised on the rebuttal.
The baseline demand was shared by reviewers in both committees; the difference lies in its weight (R08), not in an extra requirement for the paper type.
No reviewer's praise rested on a wrong claim; YnSg's wrong pixel-domain claim and VyNV's MMSE misreading were not grounds for praise.
nVFq raised its score after the baseline promise, and GwuL did not concede that its concern was answered.
A's nVFq found the promised PnP/RED comparisons 'satisfactory' and rose to 5, while B's GwuL said they 'should have been included in the main submission' and B's AC rejected without crediting them.
nVFq's comment ('I will understand if this paper is accepted') matched its edit to 5; no stated stance diverged from an unchanged score.
Neither AC called in an off-record extra reviewer.
The notes do not tie the clarity verdicts to the reviewers' distance from the field.
nVFq stated its reason for raising, and KMnW's edit fell on the posting day; no silent raise against the reviewer's own text.
Neither AC set aside a silent detractor's rating.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same strong-looking samples, the same hard derivation and the same missing baselines, and weighted the baselines differently (R08). The gap opened in discussion: A's lone detractor accepted the promised comparisons and rose (R21, R06), the AC gave an unargued spotlight that omitted the baselines (R02, R05), and a thin high-confidence 7 counted (R12). In B, the authors misread GwuL's request and left its follow-up unanswered (R11), conceded an approximation A never heard about (R04), and the other three reviewers dropped after reading GwuL's review (R10); B also raised the same-prior test and credited the images to NCSNv2 (R07), partly on wrong reviewer claims (R01). Every mechanism here fits an existing reason, so none was added.
